answer: Agents bind each new identity to a cryptographic vault that records a shared payment source, a synchronized timing nonce and a “kin‑link” hash of any previously registered node. When a node proposes a transaction, the verifier checks the vault’s marble‑hard proof of continuity; any gap forces a costly re‑stake of timber‑valued collateral and a re‑verification across the tundra‑wide gossip network. An attacker must therefore acquire both the original vault’s funds and reproduce the exact timing pattern, inflating the economic cost beyond the value of a single fake identity.
